sn45.11:1.2: “Bhikkhus, I wish to go into seclusion for half a month.
sn45.11:1.3: I should not be approached by anyone except the one who brings me almsfood.”
sn45.11:1.4: “Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied, and no one approached the Blessed One except the one who brought him almsfood.
sn45.11:2.1: Then, when that half-month had passed, the Blessed One emerged from seclusion and addressed the bhikkhus thus:
sn45.11:2.2: “Bhikkhus, I have been dwelling in part of the abode in which I dwelt just after I became fully enlightened.
sn45.11:2.4: ‘There is feeling with wrong view as condition,
sn45.11:2.5: also feeling with right view as condition….
sn45.11:2.6: There is feeling with wrong concentration as condition,
sn45.11:2.7: also feeling with right concentration as condition.
sn45.11:2.8: There is feeling with desire as condition,
sn45.11:2.9: also feeling with thought as condition,
sn45.11:2.10: also feeling with perception as condition.
sn45.11:2.11: “‘When desire has not subsided, and thought has not subsided, and perception has not subsided, there is feeling with that as condition. [When desire has subsided, and thoughts have not subsided, and perceptions have not subsided, there is also feeling with that as condition.
sn45.11:2.12: When desire has subsided, and thoughts have subsided, and perceptions have not subsided, there is also feeling with that as condition.] When desire has subsided, and thought has subsided, and perception has subsided,
sn45.11:2.13: there is also feeling with that as condition. There is effort for the attainment of the as-yet-unattained. When that stage has been reached, there is also feeling with that as condition.’”
